summary: All 7 acceptance criteria verified by code inspection and test execution.

AC3: ledger_complete_pipeline in pipeline.ts lines 455-461 computes duration_ms after setting completed_at, inside an if (pipeline.started_at) guard.

summary: Reviewed two modified files: mcp-server/src/schema/work-package.ts and mcp-server/src/tools/pipeline.ts.

work-package.ts: duration_ms: z.number().optional() added to PipelineSchema after completed_at. Position is logical. Backward-compatible (optional field — existing data validates). Pipeline TypeScript type correctly inherits duration_ms?: number via z.infer. Minor: ReworkCountsSchema uses z.number().int().nonnegative() for its count fields; duration_ms could be tightened similarly but is non-blocking.

pipeline.ts: Three-guard pattern for duration_ms computation is correct and defensive: (1) pipeline.started_at presence check, (2) !isNaN(startMs) && !isNaN(endMs) for malformed strings, (3) endMs >= startMs for clock skew. Allows duration_ms === 0 for sub-ms pipelines, which is technically correct. The endMs guard is redundant since completed_at is freshly set by now(), but the redundancy is harmless and improves self-containment.
Security: no issues — no user-controlled data flows into the timestamp parsing; worst case is NaN which is handled. Performance: two Date constructions per completion call, negligible.
Coverage gap (medium, pre-flagged by QA): no new unit tests for duration_ms behavior. Should be addressed in a follow-up tests WP.
All 7 acceptance criteria confirmed met. No blocking issues found.

comments.note: mcp-server/src/schema/work-package.ts: duration_ms uses z.number().optional() but the value is semantically always a non-negative integer (getTime() subtraction). ReworkCountsSchema uses z.number().int().nonnegative().optional() for its equivalent count fields. Consider tightening to z.number().int().nonnegative().optional() for consistency and precision. Non-blocking — existing consumers will still validate correctly.

mcp-server/src/tools/pipeline.ts: !isNaN(endMs) guard is technically redundant since pipeline.completed_at is set by now() on the immediately preceding line, so endMs is always a valid integer. The redundancy is defensive and does no harm — it makes the computation block self-contained and resilient to future reordering. Leave as-is.

mcp-server/tests/tools/pipeline.test.ts: No new tests cover duration_ms behavior (happy path, negative-duration guard, NaN guard). Pre-flagged by QA as medium-priority coverage gap. Plan step 14 calls for this coverage. Should be addressed in a dedicated tests WP.
